title: Mirabel and the Garden
premise: Vesper Reyes, a cartographer who charts the unmapped smuggler roads of the Thornfell mountains, discovers that the old gods have begun answering prayers again — and one of those answered prayers belongs to Wren, a child whose soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain. Bound by an old debt to the god Ashen-Mouth, Vesper must lead a ragged company through realms no map has ever held, stealing back the soul before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. Along the way they must choose between loyalty to the smuggler family who raised them and the truth about who sold Wren's soul in the first place. In the end, Vesper pays part of their own soul as ransom, exposes the betrayer, and returns home changed — half-mapped themselves, belonging at last to something larger than a road.
about_author: Dominic Sterling is the pen name of a former trail guide turned novelist who spent a decade leading expeditions through remote mountain ranges before turning to fantasy. Their work blends cartographic precision with folklore-soaked wonder, and 'Mirabel and the Garden' is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. While mapping a smuggler pass, Vesper witnesses a shrine ignite with impossible light — the old gods answering a prayer for the first time in centuries. The emotional beat is unease: a professional skeptic confronted with evidence their maps can't hold.

chapters.title: Wren's Empty Eyes
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They return to the village of Mirabel's Garden and find Wren, a child walking and breathing but soulless, her prayer answered in the cruelest way. The beat is guilt — Vesper passed through town weeks ago and ignored the signs.

chapters.title: Ashen-Mouth Speaks
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The god Ashen-Mouth appears in a burned chapel and reveals the debt: Vesper's mother once bargained with him, and now he calls it due. He offers the road to the court beneath the mountain. The beat is reluctant obligation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Company of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper recruits companions: Sefa, a disgraced priestess; Bramble, a thief who knows the under-road; and Old Tally, a smuggler matriarch who raised Vesper. The beat is cautious warmth — a found family assembling for an impossible errand.

chapters.title: What the Smugglers Know
chapters.summary: Old Tally's POV. Tally reveals she recognized Wren's condition instantly — because she has seen it before, decades ago. She withholds a crucial detail. The beat is dread beneath loyalty; the reader senses she is hiding complicity.

chapters.title: The Thornfell Gate
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The company crosses the first threshold into the unmapped realm, where geography obeys prayer rather than terrain. Vesper's craft begins failing them. The beat is disorientation — the expert stripped of expertise.

chapters.title: Sefa's Broken Faith
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Flashback interlude: how Sefa was cast out for insisting the gods still listened, and why she agreed to come. The beat is bitter vindication shadowed by fear that the gods are crueler than silence ever was.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In a bazaar where memories are currency, Bramble trades a cherished memory for passage, and Vesper learns the court beneath the mountain buys souls from intermediaries on the surface. The beat is mounting horror: someone above has been selling.

chapters.title: Bramble's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Bramble confesses he once ran messages for a soul-broker without knowing what he carried — and one of his deliveries went to Mirabel's Garden. The beat is shame and the fragile beginning of trust within the company.

chapters.title: The River That Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Crossing a river that shows drinkers their truest memory, Vesper sees their mother's face beside Tally's at a bargain long ago. The beat is betrayal dawning — the debt may not be Vesper's alone.

chapters.title: Tally's Confession
chapters.summary: Old Tally's POV. Cornered by the river's truth, Tally admits she brokered the sale of Wren's soul years ago to save the smuggling routes, believing the court's promises. The beat is devastating: loyalty and truth tear the company apart.

chapters.title: Exile on the Under-Road
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper banishes Tally from the company but cannot bring themselves to abandon her entirely, leaving her a marked map. The beat is grief braided with mercy — justice outside any law's reach.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The company descends into the gilded dark of the underworld court, where souls hang like lanterns and etiquette is enforced by older things than kings. The beat is awe curdling into terror.

chapters.title: An Audience of Lanterns
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper petitions the Pale Regent for Wren's soul and is refused: debts are sacred here, even unjust ones. But the Regent offers a wager instead. The beat is defiance kindling against hopeless odds.

chapters.title: The Wager of Thirteen Riddles
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The terms: answer thirteen riddles across thirteen nights or forfeit a soul of equal weight. Sefa realizes the riddles are prayers — the same ones the gods have been answering. The beat is desperate hope with a hidden design.

chapters.title: Nights One Through Nine
chapters.summary: Rotating POVs. The company endures the early riddles; Bramble sacrifices more memories, Sefa prays openly for the first time since exile, and answers begin arriving from unexpected shrines. The beat is solidarity forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Tenth Riddle Fails
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper answers wrongly and loses a decade of their own memories to the court's ledger. The beat is loss and humility — the cartographer losing the map of their own past.

chapters.title: Tally Returns
chapters.summary: Old Tally's POV. Following Vesper's marked map, Tally reaches the court and offers herself as collateral, asking only that the truth be spoken aloud before the Regent. The beat is redemption purchased at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Truth Before the Throne
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Tally confesses publicly; the court, which prizes true debts over false ones, must void the original sale as fraudulently brokered. The Regent, furious, demands a price anyway. The beat is triumph shadowed by reckoning.

chapters.title: The Price of a Soul Returned
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper volunteers half their own soul as the court's fee, and Ashen-Mouth honors the old bargain by bearing witness. The beat is sacrifice freely given — belonging proven through cost.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Night
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The company flees the collapsing court as the moon nears its thirteenth turn, carrying Wren's soul in a lantern. The final riddle answers itself: the thirteenth prayer was Vesper's own, asked long ago to belong somewhere. The beat is breathless escape into grace.

chapters.title: Mirabel in Bloom
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Wren wakes whole in Mirabel's Garden; Tally tends the village shrine in penance; Vesper, half-souled but fuller than ever, begins mapping the realm between worlds — with companions who chose to stay. The beat is quiet, earned belonging.
